title: Soft-spare buffer and grace-credit billing policy for Dedicated fleet
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a soft-spare buffer and grace-credit model to handle short-lived demand spikes on Dedicated fleets without immediately charging hard overage rates or triggering disruptive autoscaling churn. This work designs the runtime/fleet controls, autoscaler interactions, and invoice behavior for a two-tiered transient capacity mechanism: a small pre-warmed buffer (soft-spare) that customers can borrow for brief surges and a short-duration grace-credit pool that absorbs excess usage before standard overage billing applies.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes configurable soft_spare_size and grace_credit_window per customer/reservation
Autoscaler uses soft_spare as preferred borrow source before provisioning new nodes and respects per-customer cooldowns
Billing pipeline applies grace credits automatically and emits invoice line items: 'grace_credit_consumption' and 'post-grace overage' with clear prorated amounts
Console shows a per-reservation visualization (timeline) of soft-spare hits and remaining grace credits and surfaces a recommended plan when chronic consumption > 20% of reservation
E2E load test demonstrates reduced node churn (measured as node-starts-per-minute) by >= 40% for 30–90s spikes while keeping p95 latency within SLO
Feature flag gating so we can roll out to a small cohort, measure billing/latency impact, then broaden rollout
notes: Rationale: aggressive immediate scaling for short spikes creates high cost and instability (cold starts, model warmup). Soft-spare + grace credits trade a small steady allocation for smoothing and better unit economics.

Design constraints: soft-spare must be pre-warmed in ways compatible with multiple model footprints; may be implemented as mini-VMs with warmed KV caches or kept as idle containers per-gpu node depending on runtime profiling.
Fairness: when multiple customers on the same physical pool borrow soft-spare, implement proportional loaning and per-customer grace windows to avoid one tenant consuming another's buffer repeatedly.
Edge cases: multi-tenant oversubscription, long-running spike that depletes grace credits, post-grace aggressive throttling policy to protect other reservations.

Billing policy draft: first N seconds within grace_credit_window are free up to grace_credit_quota; after that, usage is billed at overage rate but smoothed with a 1-hour amortization to avoid invoice spikes. Need legal/finance review on amortization and refund mechanics.
